title: Account takeover step-up for foodpanda

success.target: Hold or better vs last quarter

already_ships: Foodpanda runs a device-graph review queue. Last quarter logged 20000 flags at a 3% takeover rate, about €900k loss on the account journey.

options.title: Keep the review queue
options.summary: Leave the device-graph queue and current step-up rules unchanged this quarter.

options.title: Step-up on new device
options.summary: Add a step-up challenge on new-device login and measure ATO rate plus false-positive cost.

options.title: Drop the queue
options.summary: Retire the manual device-graph queue and rely only on the existing password reset flow.

devils_advocate.why_fails: Step-up will bounce good riders on shared phones and inflate login drop-off in SG and HK.
devils_advocate.who_loses: Honest customers on family devices and the CX team that absorbs the extra tickets.
devils_advocate.cannot_measure: True ATO displacement versus password-reset fraud will not show in ninety days.
devils_advocate.why_not_live_control: The device-graph queue already covers the loudest takeover pattern after the fact.

recommendation.argument: The locked outcome is a funded experiment on ATO rate; only a step-up trial produces that 90-day signal.
